COURT'S OR JUDGE'S ORDERS

Rajendra Singh Negi Alias Raju
--Applicant
 Versus
State Of Uttarakhand
--Respondent
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Lalit Sharma, learned counsel with
Mr. Rajni Supyal Latwal, learned counsel for
the applicant.
2. Mr. B.C. Joshi, learned A.G.A. for the
State.
3. The instant second bal application is
moved on behalf of the applicant Rajendra
Singh Negi @ Raju for seeking regular bail in
reference to FIR dated 01.03.2026 bearing FIR
No. 03 of 2026 P.S. Dhaulchina District
Almora wherein the present applicant is
implicated and charge sheeted for the
offences punishable under Sections 109(1)
and 352 of BNS 2023 read with Section 30 of
the Arms Act.
4. The first bail application was rejected
by the Coordinate Bench on 08.05.2026 on the
ground that applicant has previous criminal
history and the offence is heinous. Now, the
second bail application is moved on the
ground that so far as criminal history is
concerned there are only two criminal cases
against him; one relates to the matrimonial
dispute wherein the applicant is acquitted by
the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate by
judgment and order dated 11.01.2012 passed
in Criminal Case No. 533 of 2012 and another
one relates to Foreigners Act and in this
regard he submits that in this case he has

UKHC010113142026
been given benefit of probation of first
offenders Act, therefore, as on date there is
no criminal antecedent. Apart from this, he
submits that in the present case there are
three injured persons and all the injuries are
simple in nature caused by pallets. Apart
from this, he submits that charge sheet has
already been filed, and, as such, there is no
need of further custodial interrogation of the
present applicant and applicant is
languishing in jail since 01.03.2026.
5. On the other side, Mr. B.C. Joshi,
learned A.GA. have not disputed that the
injuries of all the injured are simple in nature
and about criminal antecedent he has not
disputed the submissions as advanced by the
learned counsel for the applicant and
submits that in this particular case charge
sheet has already been filed.
6. After hearing the arguments of the
learned counsel for the parties and taking
into consideration that the charge sheet has
already been filed and other two criminal
cases against the applicant relate to
matrimonial one and Foreigners Act which
have already been closed, therefore, as on
date there is no criminal antecedents of the
applicant, therefore, this Court is of the view
that the applicant deserves for bail.
7. Accordingly, without expressing any
opinion on the merit of the case, the bail
application is allowed.
8. Let the applicant Rajendra Singh Negi
Alias Raju be released on bail on his
executing a personal bond and furnishing
two reliable sureties of the like amount to the
satisfaction of the court concerned.
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
21-08-2026
Parul
